items.title: Elizabeth O'Kelly Kerrigan Interview, 1958-05-04
items.q: The interviewee mentions David Dorn only in the interviewer's question ('...having any work, it first started becoming acceptable? Well... Good Society in New Orleans, have it played a part in David Dorn part in the best life?'). The interviewee does not mention David Dorn in her response, nor does

ctx.x: The blues thing? That's the thing. Yeah. Well, uh, then we had, uh, old, the Yarns Rhythm Kings, the, uh, the original Dixieland band. And I remember when I went off to school, I took two Puron records up to, uh, School of New York with them. What was that? They thought it was just noise. That was in 1923. They, they didn't appreciate it at all. And I got embarrassed after I played it once or twice and they all thought it was so horrible that I never played it anymore. Then the next year I made my debut and Puron…

Well, do you remember what your parents and your friends' parents thought about it, and what your friends thought about it when it first started, you know, having any work, it first started becoming acceptable? Well... Good Society in New Orleans, have it played a part in David Dorn part in the best life?

It was, Pierron was already established that the country club for us came there, so I don't know, it was before my time that he started playing there. And all of my friends loved it. Their parents didn't care for it too much. But, uh, I remember when I was at Newcomb, uh, that was in 1922, I guess. They, um, uh, there was a Negro, uh, sanitary near Newcomb. And, um, they would, uh, always have a band, you know, going, uh, preceding the funeral procession. And they'd play very slow duages going to the cemetery.…
